title: Closedness of the Chow immersions for a proper morphism
statement:
Let $S$ be qcqs, let $f:X\to S$ be proper, and let $\pi:\widetilde X\to X$
(proper, surjective) and $i_S:\widetilde X\to\mathbf P^n_S$ (an immersion
with $q_Si_S=f\pi$) be as in [det-chow-projective-qcqs-chow]. Then:

1. $f\pi$ is proper and $i_S$ is a closed immersion, so $f\pi$ is projective;
1. $i_X=(\pi,i_S):\widetilde X\to X\times_S\mathbf P^n_S=\mathbf P^n_X$ is a
   closed immersion, and since its composite with the projection
   $\mathbf P^n_X\to X$ is $\pi$, the morphism $\pi$ is projective.

proof.text: Both $f:X\to S$ and $\pi:\widetilde X\to X$ are proper by hypothesis. Their composite $a=f\circ\pi$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. For the finite homogeneous coordinate set defining $\mathbf P^n_S$, [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper] gives that $q_S:\mathbf P^n_S\to S$ is proper. Thus $q_S$ is separated, by the definition of properness [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Tag 01W3, lemma-composition-proper; Tag 01W1, definition-proper; projective-space properness is the cited existing node

proof.text: The identity $q_S\circ i_S=a$ in the hypotheses says exactly that $i_S$ is an $S$-morphism from the proper $S$-scheme $(\widetilde X,a)$ to the separated $S$-scheme $(\mathbf P^n_S,q_S)$. Therefore $i_S$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated]. The hypothesis already makes $i_S$ an immersion, so [lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed] makes it a closed immersion. This proves the closedness assertion of part 1.

source.place: Tag 01W6, lemma-image-proper-scheme-closed, part (2); Schemes Tag 01IQ, lemma-immersion-when-closed (schemes.tex)

proof.text: We follow the graph factorization of unit sk-thm-chow-projective, step 2. Since $f$ is proper it is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-change-of-base-closed-immersion] with the two maps to $X$ equal to $\pi:\widetilde X\to X$ and $\mathrm{id}_X:X\to X$, and with the separated map $X\to S$ equal to $f$. It gives a closed immersion $\widetilde X\times_X X\to\widetilde X\times_S X$. The first projection identifies $\widetilde X\times_X X$ with $\widetilde X$: its inverse is $(\mathrm{id},\pi)$, and the two inverse identities follow by comparing projections [def-pc-fibre-product]. Under this identification the displayed closed immersion is the graph $\Gamma_\pi=(\mathrm{id},\pi):\widetilde X\to\widetilde X\times_S X$. Thus this graph is closed. This is precisely the diagonal-base-change graph argument carried by the cited statement.

Let $b=i_S\times_S\mathrm{id}_X:\widetilde X\times_S X\to\mathbf P^n_S\times_S X$. This is the base change of the closed immersion $i_S$ along the first projection $\mathbf P^n_S\times_S X\to\mathbf P^n_S$, so it is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. To check the base-change identification, for any scheme $T$ a map into its pullback consists of $z:T\to\widetilde X$ and $(p,x):T\to\mathbf P^n_S\times_S X$ with $i_Sz=p$; substituting $p=i_Sz$ leaves exactly a pair $(z,x)$ with $az=fx$, the universal property of $\widetilde X\times_S X$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The projection is then the stated map $b$.

source.place: Tag 01JY, lemma-base-change-immersion; equivalently Morphisms Tag 01QR, lemma-base-change-closed-immersion (morphisms.tex)

proof.text: The composite $b\circ\Gamma_\pi$ is a closed immersion by the composition clause of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-products]. Its two components in $\mathbf P^n_S\times_S X$ are $i_S$ and $\pi$, as follows by composing the defining projections [def-pc-fibre-product]. Interchanging the projections therefore identifies it with $(\pi,i_S):\widetilde X\to X\times_S\mathbf P^n_S$. This target is canonically $\mathbf P^n_X$ with its projection to $X$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]: writing $P=\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$, a map to $X\times_S(S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}P)$ consists of maps $x:T\to X$, $s:T\to S$, $p:T\to P$ with $s=fx$ and the compatibility over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$; eliminating $s$ gives exactly a map to $X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}P$. These assignments are inverse and preserve the projection to $X$, by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Consequently $i_X$ is a closed immersion and its composite with $q_X:\mathbf P^n_X\to X$ is $\pi$.

source.place: Tag 02V0, lemma-composition-immersion, closed-immersion clause; Tag 01JP, definition-fibre-product; projective space is the cited definition

proof.text: We have the two factorizations $a=q_S\circ i_S$ and $\pi=q_X\circ i_X$ through closed immersions into the projective spaces $\mathbf P^n_S=\mathbf P(n;S)$ and $\mathbf P^n_X=\mathbf P(n;X)$ on the finite homogeneous index set $n$, by steps 2 and 5. To match the integer indexing of [def-pc-projective-morphism], where $\mathbf P^r_S$ is $\mathbf P(\{0,\dots,r\};S)$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], reindex. If $n$ has $r+1\geq1$ elements, a bijection $n\cong\{0,\dots,r\}$ renames the variables, giving an isomorphism of graded rings $\mathbf Z[T_i:i\in n]\cong\mathbf Z[T_0,\dots,T_r]$, hence of their Proj, hence (base changing along $S\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, resp. $X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$) an isomorphism $\mathbf P(n;S)\cong\mathbf P^r_S$ over $S$, resp. $\mathbf P(n;X)\cong\mathbf P^r_X$ over $X$. A closed immersion followed by an isomorphism is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. If $n=\emptyset$, the graded ring $\mathbf Z$ sits in degree $0$, so its Proj, and hence $\mathbf P(\emptyset;S)$, is empty; then $\widetilde X$ is empty, since $i_S$ maps it into the empty scheme, and the empty morphisms $\widetilde X\to\mathbf P^0_S$ and $\widetilde X\to\mathbf P^0_X$ are closed immersions (empty closed image, and $\mathcal O\to0$ is surjective) over $S$, resp. $X$. These are exactly the H-projective factorizations of [def-pc-projective-morphism]. For the additional quasi-compactness in that node's projective convention, $a$ is proper by step 1 and $\pi$ is proper by hypothesis. Proper morphisms are of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism], and finite type includes quasi-compactness [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Both morphisms are thus projective in the stated convention, giving every remaining clause.

source.place: Tag 01W8, definition-projective, H-projective convention; Tag 01W1, definition-proper; finite type includes quasi-compactness; reindexing of homogeneous coordinates is the cited definition of P(n;S)
